main.description: An encrypted file or document stored in the personal cloud. The actual content is an encrypted blob; this record holds the encryption envelope and encrypted metadata. All document metadata (name, MIME type, size, tags, description) is encrypted inside encryptedMetadata using the same content key as the blob.

opakeVersion.description: Schema version for the at.opake.* namespace. Clients should reject records with a version they do not understand.

blob.description: The encrypted file content, uploaded via com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob. The PDS stores this as opaque bytes. MimeType on the blob itself will be 'application/octet-stream'.

encryption.description: How to decrypt the blob. Either a full encryption envelope (with per-document wrapped keys) or a keyring reference (for group-based access).

supersedes.description: AT-URI of an earlier document this record supersedes, if any. Load-bearing: it feeds the indexer's additive-advance authority check for editor swaps and carries a verified content pin (`supersedesCid`). Absent on a fresh document.

supersedesCid.description: CID of the exact predecessor record named by `supersedes` — the immediate prior document this record supersedes. Required whenever `supersedes` is present (enforced at the app layer pre-v1). Names the immediate predecessor only and is never copied through. At v1, readers compare it against the CID a host reports for the fetched predecessor (not a hash recomputed from bytes), so it detects CID disagreement between honest hosts; true byte-level tamper-evidence is deferred to replication-tier work.

lineage.description: AT-URI of this document chain's genesis record — the document's stable object identity. Absent on a genesis document, which identifies itself. Present on every supersede, and never changing across one. Content and metadata ciphertexts are AEAD-bound to this anchor.

workspaceId.description: Genesis keyring URI of the workspace this document belongs to. Absent on cabinet documents. Carried explicitly so any reader can resolve workspace identity without walking the keyring chain back to genesis.

directEncryption.description: Encryption where the content key is wrapped directly to one or more DIDs. Used for private files or ad-hoc sharing.

keyringEncryption.description: Encryption where the content key is wrapped under a keyring's group key. Anyone with access to the keyring can decrypt.

algo.description: Symmetric algorithm used for content encryption.
